Empirical Research Plan: Mandated Political Representation and Redistributive Policy in Indian States, 1960-1992
==========================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Method: Staggered Difference-in-Differences (two-way fixed effects) complemented by an event–study specification.

Why it fits:
• “Treatment” (the share of constituencies reserved for SCs or STs) changes discretely when new census figures are written into law by the national Delimitation Commission.  
• The timing and size of these changes are determined by a constitutional rule, not by contemporaneous state-level politics.  
• We observe states before and after each reservation revision as well as states whose shares do not change in a given year, yielding a classical DID set-up with plausibly exogenous, staggered treatment.  
• An event study around the first year the new seat shares are used in a state election allows us to inspect pre-trends and dynamic effects.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
  T_it  ≡  % of seats in state i’s legislative assembly reserved for (a) Scheduled Castes or (b) Scheduled Tribes in year t.  
  We will estimate separate equations for SC reservations and ST reservations and, where useful, include both simultaneously.

Control (counterfactual) group  
• State-years in which the reservation share has not yet changed serve as controls for treated state-years.  
• In intensity form, the counterfactual is implicitly “zero additional reserved seats” in a given year.

Treatment timing / event date  
• Event year 0 = first fiscal year in which a state’s assembly elected under the new reservation shares is in office (typically the fiscal year after the first election following a delimitation order).  
• Leads (t < 0) and lags (t ≥ 0) of this event define the event-study dummies.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends: Absent a change in reservation shares, treated and untreated states would have followed the same trend in redistributive policy outcomes.  
 Plausibility: Reservation changes are federally mandated and infrequent, making it unlikely that states that happen to receive larger revisions were on systematically different expenditure trajectories. Still, we will test visually with pre-period event-study coefficients and add state-specific linear trends.

A2. Exogenous timing and magnitude: The Delimitation Commission follows census-based formulas; states cannot influence the timing or size of revisions.  
 Plausibility: Constitutional provisions and a national commission insulate the process from state politics, supporting exogeneity.

A3. Stable unit treatment value (SUTVA): A change in one state’s reservation share does not directly affect another state’s spending.  
 Plausibility: States have fiscal autonomy and budgets are largely independent, so cross-state spillovers are minimal.

A4. No anticipatory effects: State governments do not systematically alter spending before the first election under the new seat shares.  
 Plausibility: Delimitation orders are announced fairly close to elections and are implemented by an external agency, limiting strategic pre-adjustment. We will include leads to test this.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Main Threats & Remedies
--------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Correlation with underlying SC/ST population changes  
 • Growing SC populations could independently raise demand for targeted spending.  
 Remedy: Control flexibly for current and lagged SC (or ST) population shares and their interactions with year dummies; include state-specific linear or quadratic trends.

T2. Heterogeneous treatment timing and two-way FE bias (Goodman-Bacon issues)  
 Remedy: (i) Use recent estimators robust to staggered adoption (e.g., Callaway-Sant’Anna or Sun-Abraham in R package “fixest” or “did”). (ii) Present both conventional TWFE and heterogeneity-robust estimates.

T3. Contemporaneous political shocks (e.g., Emergency period 1975-77)  
 Remedy: Include election-year dummy, national-level year fixed effects, and state-specific time trends; run robustness checks dropping years with national shocks.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
--------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# ---- 0. Packages ----
library(data.table)   # fast data
library(fixest)       # TWFE and Sun-Abraham DID
library(did)          # Callaway-Sant’Anna
library(ggplot2)

# ---- 1. Load Data ----
dt <- fread("indian_states_1960_1992.csv")  # one row per state-year

# ---- 2. Construct Variables ----
dt[, year  := as.integer(year)]
dt[, post_delim_sc := ifelse(year >= sc_delim_year, 1, 0)]  # 1 if after new SC reservation in force
dt[, post_delim_st := ifelse(year >= st_delim_year, 1, 0)]

# Continuous treatment variables
dt[, sc_reserve_share := sc_reserved_seats / total_seats]
dt[, st_reserve_share := st_reserved_seats / total_seats]

# Outcomes (examples)
y_vars <- c("real_pc_total_exp", "edu_budget_share",
            "scst_welfare_share", "scst_job_quota_share")

# ---- 3. Main TWFE Specification ----
# Equation:  Y_it = β * sc_reserve_share_it + γX_it + δ_i + λ_t + ε_it
est <- feols(
  scst_welfare_share ~ sc_reserve_share + 
    log(real_pc_income) + gini + election_year +
    i(year, state_pop_share_sc) | state + year,
  data = dt, cluster = "state"
)
summary(est)

# ---- 4. Event-Study (Sun & Abraham style) ----
# Build relative time to first SC reservation change
dt[, rel_time_sc := year - sc_delim_year]      # can be negative
dt[, rel_time_sc := fifelse(abs(rel_time_sc) > 10, 10*sign(rel_time_sc), rel_time_sc)]

es <- feols(
  scst_welfare_share ~ sunab(sc_delim_year, year, ref = -1) +
    log(real_pc_income) + gini | state + year,
  data = dt, cluster = "state"
)
iplot(es)  # quick visual of dynamics

# ---- 5. Heterogeneity-robust DID (Callaway-Sant’Anna) ----
cs <- att_gt(yname = "scst_welfare_share",
             tname = "year",
             idname = "state",
             gname = "sc_delim_year",
             xformla = ~ log(real_pc_income) + gini,
             data = dt)
agg_effect <- aggte(cs, type = "dynamic")
summary(agg_effect)

# ---- 6. Robustness Check: Drop National-Shock Years ----
dt_rob <- dt[!(year %in% 1975:1977)]
est_rob <- update(est, data = dt_rob)
etable(est, est_rob, se = "cluster")

# (Additional checks could include placebo on pre-period leads,
# instrumenting reserved share with lagged census share, etc.)
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Theory predicts that legislators who are members of SC/ST groups will push for policies favoring their constituencies, especially when electoral incentives (same electorate but minority candidates) still require broad support.

Prior expectations:  
• A 1-percentage-point increase in the share of seats reserved for SCs is expected to raise the SC-/ST-targeted welfare spending share by roughly 0.05–0.10 pp (i.e., elasticity of 0.05–0.10).  
• Total per-capita spending may rise modestly (if lobbying boosts spending) or remain flat (if composition shifts from other programs).  
• Land-reform passage likelihood and government-job quotas should rise with SC/ST seat shares.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (Difference-in-Differences)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
C1: No anticipatory behavior……………………………… 1  
C2: Parallel pre-treatment trends………………………… 0.5 (to be verified)  
C3: Exogenous treatment timing…………………………… 1  
C4: No interference across units (SUTVA)…………… 0.5  
C5: Correct functional form & controls………………… 1  

Total (out of 5): 4/5 – credible but dependent on confirmed parallel trends and minimal spillovers.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
End of Plan
